subject: tu:game/audio/dcsdrv
value:
SECOND CONFIRMATION OF THE 'READ THE DIRECTION' RULE, AND A REUSABLE FINGERPRINT FOR IDENTIFYING AN UNCLAIMED .data RANGE WITHOUT GUESSING. dcsdrv's flip-blocking data line was `target 0x0 vs ours 0xB8`, the same direction as movieplayer's: splits.txt claimed only extab/extabindex/.text, our object's bytes were already correct, and nothing needed to be emitted or spelled. Fix: one line, `.data start:0x801295C8 end:0x80129680`. Result: section 100.0% bytes equal, +184 matched data bytes, both datadiff modes exit 0.

THE FINGERPRINT, which cost no build and should be the default method for any `target 0x0 vs ours N` data line. Our object's .data consisted of exactly two local objects, @51 (size 0x50) and @230 (size 0x68), and `objdump -r --section=.data` showed every one of their 46 words is an R_PPC_ADDR32 into this TU's own .text — i.e. the whole section is compiler-generated switch jumptables, one per switch statement, in source order (dcsMain's 20-entry table, then dcsHandleRequest's 26-entry table). A grep of symbols.txt for the .data neighbourhood then found `jumptable_801295C8 size:0x50` immediately followed by `jumptable_80129618 size:0x68`, i.e. a CONTIGUOUS pair whose sizes and ORDER match ours exactly and whose total is 0xB8 = our section size. Two independent corroborations followed: the split listing's `.4byte dcsMain+0x1F4 ...` / `.4byte dcsHandleRequest+0x658 ...` addend sequences are entry-for-entry identical to our relocation addends; and link order agrees (the range sits inside the unclaimed .data gap 0x801286D0..0x80129710 whose neighbours follow the same .text order, with cardutil claiming 0x80129710 immediately above and movieplayer's vtable block 0x8012968C..0x80129710 directly below it). SIZE-AND-ORDER MATCH OF A JUMPTABLE RUN IS A SUFFICIENT IDENTIFICATION: a TU's jumptables are emitted one per switch in source order and are named `jumptable_<ADDR>` with declared sizes in symbols.txt, so matching the multiset of sizes in order against our own local .data objects locates the range uniquely, before any configure/ninja cycle.

BOUNDARY: the claim is exactly symbol-covered (0x80129680 = jumptable_80129618 + 0x68), so no trailing pad exists and the claim-slack law does not arise in either of its cases. Neighbouring symbols lbl_80129588 (ends exactly at our start) and lbl_80129680 (begins exactly at our end) belong to adjacent TUs and must NOT be swept into the claim.

TU STATUS AFTER THIS: dcsdrv's data gate is fully closed and dcsInit/dcsMain measure real 0; the TU flip remains blocked by dcsHandleRequest alone (real 144), whose residual is recorded in attempt.DC_dcshandlerequest-jumptable-settled-and-webfrank-barred.20260901.v1.
